advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/document behavior when a deferred maintenance repack legitimately exceeds _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (repeated foreground SIGKILL mid-repack on every write); consider detaching or backing off the repack instead of retrying it foreground each write.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py:230: 'the roomier ``_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT`` watchdog — a hung repack fails this step cleanly.'

run_auto_maintenance returns run_git_bounded(..., 'maintenance','run','--auto', timeout=_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT); run_git_bounded folds TimeoutExpired into rc-124 after the child is SIGKILLed by subprocess.run's timeout

'--auto preserves git's threshold check, so it is a cheap no-op until the store actually needs a repack' — but once past threshold it repeats the full repack on every write until one completes within 120s
The commit message itself notes 'Raising the timeout only moves the cliff' — the same logic applies to the 120s deferred bound on a sufficiently large store
advisory.finding: The deferred maintenance repack still runs FOREGROUND under the write lock bounded by _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (120s). On a store whose full repack legitimately exceeds 120s, run_auto_maintenance returns rc-124 (SIGKILL mid-repack) — and since the loose objects persist, EVERY subsequent write re-triggers the same foreground repack attempt and can again be killed mid-repack. This re-introduces the interrupted-repack corruption ADR 0051 exists to prevent; the fix moves the cliff from _GIT_TIMEOUT (30s) to _LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT (120s) rather than eliminating it.
scenarios: A very large mature store where a full repack exceeds 120s
Repeated writes each re-attempt (and re-kill) the same over-budget foreground repack under the lock

src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:203 comment: 'rebar's own write lock (which only serialises writes WITHIN one clone) does not stop a concurrent rebar process … from colliding on git's OWN .git/index.lock'
txn._git and event_append route index-mutating ops through run_git_write / _with_index_lock_retry for exactly this contention
advisory.finding: run_auto_maintenance issues 'git maintenance run --auto' via run_git_bounded, which (unlike run_git_write used by every other lock-held git op in txn.py/event_append) does NOT compose the index.lock self-heal or the transient runner-FS fault retry. Under the shared tickets worktree the write lock only serialises within one clone, so a peer's index.lock or a runner-FS blip fails the maintenance step where the sibling commit path would have self-healed.
scenarios: Concurrent rebar peers on the shared worktree during the deferred maintenance step

The bd66 regression test would still pass if `_deferred_maintenance(tracker)` were deleted entirely (its success assertion depends only on the `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` suppression), so a regression that stopped deferring maintenance — letting loose objects accumulate unbounded off the commit path — would go undetected.
